issues.legal_issue: A person who died before migrating to India or abandoning land because of disturbances or partition does not qualify as a displaced person or refugee for replacement-land allotment.
material_facts: The deceased owned agricultural land in territory that became part of Pakistan.
He died in India during an ordinary business visit, before partition and before the disturbances led to the abandonment of the land.
His sons migrated to India after partition and later claimed replacement land for the abandoned property.
issues.conclusion: The deceased did not qualify as a displaced person or refugee because he died before migrating or abandoning his land as a result of disturbances, fear of disturbances, or partition.
issues.legal_principle: Paragraph 2(e) of the Custodian’s notification of July 8, 1949, issued under the East Punjab Evacuees (Administration of Property) Act, 1947, and section 2(d) of the East Punjab Refugees (Registration of Land Claims) Act, 1948, define the relevant status by reference to migration or abandonment caused by disturbances, fear of disturbances, or partition. The definition of displaced person in section 2(c) of the East Punjab Displaced Persons (Land Resettlement) Act, 1949, likewise requires abandonment for those reasons.

predicates.replacement_land_allotment_case: The proceeding concerns eligibility for allotment of replacement land on account of property left behind during displacement.
predicates.owned_land_in_affected_territory: The person owned land in territory from which people left or abandoned property because of disturbances, fear of disturbances, or partition.
predicates.died_before_displacement_migration: The person died before migrating or abandoning the land as a result of disturbances, fear of disturbances, or partition.
predicates.deceased_does_not_qualify_as_displaced_l: A person who died before displacement does not qualify as a displaced landholder for replacement-land allotment.

issues.definition: When a replacement-land allotment proceeding concerns land in an affected territory and its owner died before displacement migration, that owner does not qualify as a displaced landholder.

issues.legal_issue: An administrative instruction to record allotment in the name of a deceased landholder applies only when that person became displaced before dying and died before allotment; it cannot extend statutory eligibility to someone who died before becoming displaced.
material_facts: The deceased’s name remained in the revenue records as owner of the land left behind.
The deceased had died before partition and before becoming a displaced landholder.
The land allotment authorities relied on an administrative manual to cancel part of the heirs’ allotment and maintained that allotment had to be made in the deceased’s name.
The manual was an administrative instruction and did not have statutory authority.
issues.conclusion: The manual’s direction did not apply because the deceased had not become a displaced landholder before his death; the revenue entry and lack of mutation did not make him eligible for allotment.
issues.legal_principle: Statutory provisions prevail over inconsistent executive or administrative instructions. The Court cited Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer for the principle that executive action is subject to law, and applied the rule of law to administrative action. Paragraph 17 of Tarlok Singh’s Land Resettlement Manual is consistent with the governing statutes only when read as covering a landholder who became a displaced person under paragraph 2(e) of the July 8, 1949 notification or the relevant statutory definitions and died before allotment. The Manual does not apply to someone who died before becoming displaced.

rule.if: replacement_land_allotment_case and administrative_instruction_controls_allotment_name and revenue_records_name_deceased and deceased_died_before_becoming_displaced

predicates.replacement_land_allotment_case: The proceeding concerns allotment of replacement land after property was left behind during displacement.
predicates.administrative_instruction_controls_allo: An authority relies on an administrative instruction that directs allotment to be recorded in a deceased landholder’s name.
predicates.revenue_records_name_deceased: The land records continue to identify the deceased person as owner, and the heirs’ names have not been entered by mutation.
predicates.deceased_died_before_becoming_displaced: The landholder died before migrating or abandoning the land as a result of disturbances, fear of disturbances, or partition.
predicates.administrative_instruction_cannot_requir: An administrative instruction cannot require allotment in the deceased person’s name when that person had not become displaced before dying.

issues.definition: If an allotment authority relies on an administrative instruction and the records name a person who died before becoming displaced, the instruction cannot require allotment in that person’s name.
